title: Sustainable Finance and ESG Supervision
summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess ESG and climate risk, sustainability disclosures and product claims, and to integrate sustainable finance into day-to-day supervision.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to integrate sustainability risk into day-to-day supervision: assessing how firms identify and manage ESG and climate risk, testing disclosures and product claims, and telling genuine integration apart from greenwashing.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a practical understanding of environmental, social and governance risks, the disclosure and reporting frameworks that apply to them, and the tools to assess whether firms' claims match reality. Participants leave able to review sustainability risk assessments, challenge governance, product design and disclosures, identify greenwashing and embed sustainability in routine supervisory work.
sections.What It Covers: Sustainable finance and ESG risk foundations, climate and nature-related financial risk, the regulatory and disclosure landscape, sustainability reporting standards and ESG data, sustainability risk assessment, governance and risk management, product governance and labelling, greenwashing and greenbleaching, climate scenario analysis, and integrating sustainability into supervision.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors in banking, insurance, investment funds, investment services and pensions
Sustainable finance, policy and risk specialists supporting supervisory teams
Authorisation and product teams reviewing sustainability-related products and disclosures
Learning Objectives: Explain the key environmental, social and governance risks and how they affect financial products and services
Describe the main sustainable finance disclosure, taxonomy and reporting frameworks and how they interact
Assess a firm's sustainability risk assessment, governance and risk management
Evaluate product governance, labelling and disclosures for substance and consistency
Identify greenwashing and greenbleaching and select a proportionate supervisory response
Design an approach for integrating sustainable finance into day-to-day supervision
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day workshops. Each module combines a technical briefing with class discussion, case studies and supervisory question exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's sectors and needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision or risk assessment is helpful. No prior knowledge of sustainable finance or ESG is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Principles for the Effective Management and Supervision of Climate-related Financial Risks (2022)
NGFS, Guide for Supervisors: Integrating Climate-related and Environmental Risks into Prudential Supervision (2020)
ISSB, IFRS S1 General Requirements and IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures (2023)
IOSCO, Recommendations on Sustainability-Related Practices, Policies, Procedures and Disclosure in Asset Management (2021)

modules.title: Sustainable Finance and ESG Risk Foundations
modules.summary: An introduction to sustainable finance, the environmental, social and governance risks that affect financial products and services, and why sustainability has become a supervisory concern.
objectives: Explain the scope of sustainable finance and the main ESG risk categories
Distinguish sustainability risks to firms from firms' impacts on sustainability factors
Identify how ESG risks translate into credit, market, liquidity, operational and conduct risk
syllabus: Sustainable finance, ESG integration and impact investing: key terms
Environmental, social and governance risk categories with examples
Single and double materiality
Green, social and sustainability-linked bonds and loans

modules.title: Climate and Nature-Related Financial Risks
modules.summary: How physical and transition risks arising from climate change and nature loss reach firms' balance sheets and business models, and the transmission channels supervisors need to understand.
objectives: Explain physical and transition risk and their transmission channels
Analyse sector and portfolio exposures to climate and nature-related risk
Assess the time horizon and uncertainty challenges in measuring these risks
syllabus: Physical risk: acute and chronic hazards
Transition risk: policy, technology, market and litigation drivers
Nature-related risks and biodiversity loss
NGFS, Basel Committee and IAIS work on climate-related financial risk

modules.title: The Sustainable Finance Regulatory Landscape
modules.summary: The building blocks of sustainable finance regulation, from taxonomies and disclosure regimes to corporate due diligence, and how international standards shape national and regional approaches.
objectives: Describe the main types of sustainable finance regulation and their objectives
Explain how taxonomies, product disclosure and corporate reporting regimes interact
Analyse the direction of travel in sustainable finance regulation
syllabus: Sustainable finance taxonomies and their use in classification
Product-level and entity-level sustainability disclosure regimes
Corporate sustainability reporting and due diligence obligations
International coordination: FSB, IOSCO, NGFS and G20 roadmaps

modules.title: Sustainability Reporting Standards and ESG Data
modules.summary: How corporate sustainability reporting standards compare, the quality and limits of ESG data, ratings and scores, and what this means for firms relying on them.
objectives: Compare the ISSB standards with other international sustainability reporting frameworks
Evaluate the reliability and limits of ESG data, ratings and scoring methodologies
Assess how firms govern their use of third-party ESG data
syllabus: ISSB standards and their foundations in TCFD
Regional reporting standards and interoperability
ESG ratings and scores: methodologies, divergence and conflicts
Data gaps, estimates and assurance of sustainability information

modules.title: Sustainability Risk Assessment in Supervised Entities
modules.summary: How firms should identify, measure and assess sustainability risks, and how supervisors review the quality of a sustainability risk assessment and its links to the firm's business model.
objectives: Describe the process of undertaking a sustainability risk assessment
Assess whether a firm's materiality assessment is complete and evidence-based
Identify the implications of sustainability risk for different types of supervised entity
syllabus: Risk identification, materiality assessment and heatmaps
Linking sustainability risk to the business model and strategy
Sector differences: banks, insurers, asset managers and pension schemes
Case study: reviewing a firm's sustainability risk assessment

modules.title: ESG Governance and Risk Management in Firms
modules.summary: How boards and management should govern sustainability risk, embed it in risk appetite and the three lines of defence, and develop credible transition plans.
objectives: Assess board oversight and accountability for sustainability risk
Evaluate how sustainability risk is embedded in risk appetite, policies and controls
Challenge the credibility of a firm's transition plan and targets
syllabus: Board skills, accountability and remuneration links
Risk appetite, limits and integration into the three lines of defence
Transition plans: targets, interim milestones and implementation
Red flags and supervisory questions on ESG governance

modules.title: Product Governance, Labelling and Disclosure
modules.summary: How sustainability features are designed into products, labelled and disclosed to investors and customers, and how supervisors test whether product claims are substantiated.
objectives: Explain sustainability product categories, labels and disclosure expectations
Assess product governance, target market and investment process for sustainability claims
Evaluate consistency between pre-contractual, periodic and marketing disclosures
syllabus: Sustainability product categories and labelling regimes
Investment process evidence: exclusions, stewardship and engagement
Sustainability preferences in suitability and distribution
Exercise: reviewing a fund's sustainability disclosures

modules.title: Greenwashing and Greenbleaching
modules.summary: How misleading sustainability claims arise at entity, product and marketing level, why some firms understate their credentials, and the supervisory and enforcement tools for addressing both.
objectives: Identify common forms of greenwashing and greenbleaching
Apply red-flag indicators to disclosures, names and marketing materials
Evaluate proportionate supervisory and enforcement responses
syllabus: Definitions and typologies of greenwashing across the investment chain
Greenbleaching and the incentives to understate sustainability features
Fund names, marketing claims and social media
Case studies: supervisory findings and enforcement outcomes

modules.title: Climate Scenario Analysis and Stress Testing
modules.summary: How firms and authorities use climate scenarios and stress tests to explore long-horizon risks, and how supervisors judge the quality and use of firms' scenario analysis.
objectives: Explain the design and purpose of climate scenario analysis and stress testing
Assess the assumptions, data and limitations of a firm's scenario analysis
Evaluate how scenario results feed into strategy, capital and risk management
syllabus: NGFS scenarios and their use by firms and authorities
Top-down and bottom-up exercises: design choices and lessons learned
Model limitations, data gaps and proportionality for smaller firms
Using results in capital planning and risk appetite

modules.title: Integrating Sustainable Finance into Day-to-Day Supervision
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a practical approach for embedding sustainability in risk assessment, reviews, inspections and authorisation, and anticipates future changes to the regulatory framework.
objectives: Apply sustainability considerations to routine supervisory activity across sectors
Prioritise sustainability supervision using a risk-based approach
Design an action plan for the authority's sustainable finance supervision
syllabus: Sustainability in risk assessment frameworks, reviews and inspections
Thematic reviews, data requests and supervisory expectations
Future developments in sustainable finance regulation
Workshop: the authority's sustainable finance supervision action plan

related.title: Agentic Finance for Supervisors
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to understand and supervise AI agents that transact and make financial decisions, from agent identity to payments and liability.

related.title: AI Governance for Supervisors
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess firms' AI governance, model and fairness risk, and to shape the authority's approach to AI supervision.

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.

related.title: Big Tech, Embedded Finance and Open Finance
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping supervisors to assess big tech, embedded finance and open finance models, and their concentration, conduct and operational risks.

related.title: Capital Markets and Investment Services Supervision
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to oversee investment firms, trading venues and issuers, from client conduct and client assets to algorithmic trading and market abuse.

related.title: Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals
related.summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving supervisors a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks they must supervise.
